policy: Prospective per-journal activation dates; multi-ISSN Crossref online/published/created union plus OpenAlex union; default three-calendar-day Beijing primary semantic-review window, seven-calendar-day machine-only multi-source safety tail (including Crossref created/deposit rescue and OpenAlex), automatic catch-up from the first unverified date when verifiedThrough falls behind, and closure-day source-coverage regression detection. Repository and deployed gallery DOI sets are unioned to avoid deployment-race false positives. Every DOI difference remains reviewable: deterministic screening only assigns review priority and never silently excludes a new missing record. Publisher TOC/Early View/ASAP is an additional assistant-side closure check when available.

closure.note: Machine audit never advances verifiedThrough by itself. Persisted assistant exclusions are treated as resolved; accepted papers must exist in repository/site data, pending items remain unresolved, publisher sources must be cross-checked where available, critical source failures must be zero, and closure-day Crossref/OpenAlex coverage must not show a severe one-family collapse.

missingCandidates.title: Anti-Kasha fluorescence and persistent room-temperature phosphorescence from a nearly flat non-symmetric polycyclic hydrocarbon
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are molecular frameworks that enable the development of efficient emitters owing to their extensive conjugation and rigid structure. Here, we introduce monohomotruxene (MHTX), designed by reducing the symmetry of homotruxene (HTX) and truxene (TX). This partial planarization greatly enhances the complex photophysics over symmetric, triply twisted HTX, substantially increasing the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), a result we attribute to its enhanced molecular rigidity and symmetry breaking. MHTX displays an unconventional violation of Kasha’s rule, yielding excitation-dependent dual emission. Excitation of the S 2 state under anaerobic conditions produces intense, 455–480 nm, ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP), lasting over 12 s at room temperature. In contrast, excitation into the S 1 state yields prompt fluorescence and weak delayed fluorescence (DF) by triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) in the neat film. Aggregate species also present a complex emissive behavior with weak orange phosphorescence and TTA-DF. These findings establish MHTX as a promising emissive scaffold, highlighting the potential for accessing complex excited-state dynamics and advanced photophysical functionalities.
